{{Short description|Species of aquatic plant}} {{no footnotes|date=March 2013}} {{Speciesbox |image = Starr_980601-1501_Hydrocotyle_verticillata.jpg |status = LC |status_system = IUCN3.1 |status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Bárrios, S. |author2=Copeland, A. |year=2021 |title=''Hydrocotyle verticillata'' |article-number=e.T19620823A192133822 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2021-3.RLTS.T19620823A192133822.en |access-date=26 November 2022}} |genus = Hydrocotyle |species = verticillata |authority = [[Thunb.]] }} '''''Hydrocotyle verticillata''''', also known as '''whorled pennywort''', '''whorled marshpennywort''' or '''shield pennywort''', is a [[flowering plant]] found in South and North America and the West Indies. Its creeping habit and unusual [[leaves]] give it its common names. It grows in places that are marshy, boggy, or even wet.
''Hydrocotyle verticillata'' is used in [[Aquarium|aquaria]], where it is undemanding; it does prefer a good [[substrate (biology)|substrate]], however, and at least moderate light. It benefits from additional [[carbon dioxide]].
